headline: 3 die in Mexico City as fans crowd streets for World Cup celebrations
summary: Three people died from suffocation after thousands of fans gathered to celebrate Mexico's 2-0 victory over Ecuador.
details: Three people died from suffocation as thousands of fans crowded Mexico City streets during World Cup celebrations, according to the capital's health secretariat.
The deaths occurred near the Angel of Independence landmark, where fans had gathered to celebrate Mexico's 2-0 victory over Ecuador in the round of 32.
Emergency teams treated three unconscious people at different locations around Paseo de la Reforma, the city's most emblematic boulevard.
The victims included a 44-year-old man and a 19-year-old woman who died after resuscitation efforts, and a 48-year-old woman who died in the hospital after suffering asphyxiation.
Mayor Clara Brugada expressed her condolences to the families and urged citizens to celebrate with responsibility, care, and empathy.
The celebrations followed Mexico's first World Cup knockout victory in 40 years, achieved at the Azteca Stadium, sending the co-hosts into the last 16.
caption:
Three people died from suffocation in Mexico City as thousands of fans crowded the streets to celebrate a historic World Cup win.

Three people died from suffocation as thousands of fans crowded Mexico City streets during World Cup celebrations, according to the capital's health secretariat.

The deaths occurred near the Angel of Independence landmark, where fans had gathered to celebrate Mexico's 2-0 victory over Ecuador in the round of 32.

Emergency teams treated three unconscious people at different locations around Paseo de la Reforma, the city's most emblematic boulevard.

The victims included a 44-year-old man and a 19-year-old woman who died after resuscitation efforts, and a 48-year-old woman who died in the hospital after suffering asphyxiation.

Mayor Clara Brugada expressed her condolences to the families and urged citizens to celebrate with responsibility, care, and empathy.

The celebrations followed Mexico's first World Cup knockout victory in 40 years, achieved at the Azteca Stadium, sending the co-hosts into the last 16.

headline_marked: Police to use [[body cameras at HSC centres]] to ensure security
headline: Police to use body cameras at HSC centres to ensure security
summary: Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced the move to prevent outsiders from entering exam centres as 1.27 million students sit for the exams.
details: Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced that police officers on duty at Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examination centres will use body cameras to ensure security.
The move is specifically aimed at preventing the entry of unauthorized outsiders into the examination centres to maintain a controlled environment.
A total of 1,270,583 students are appearing for their HSC and equivalent examinations across 2,697 centres nationwide.
The written examinations for the nine general boards and the Madrasah board are scheduled to end on August 8, while practical examinations will continue until August 15.
The minister also issued a stern warning against the spread of misleading information regarding the exams on social media.
Milon stated that cybersecurity laws will be used to take strict legal action against anyone circulating false news to prevent confusion among students.
caption:
Police will now wear body cameras at HSC exam centres to stop outsiders from entering.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced that police officers on duty at Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examination centres will use body cameras to ensure security.

The move is specifically aimed at preventing the entry of unauthorized outsiders into the examination centres to maintain a controlled environment.

A total of 1,270,583 students are appearing for their HSC and equivalent examinations across 2,697 centres nationwide.

The written examinations for the nine general boards and the Madrasah board are scheduled to end on August 8, while practical examinations will continue until August 15.

The minister also issued a stern warning against the spread of misleading information regarding the exams on social media.

Milon stated that cybersecurity laws will be used to take strict legal action against anyone circulating false news to prevent confusion among students.

#HSC #Bangladesh #Education #ExamSecurity #StudentLife

Source: Somoy News, bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV
